raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Two independent bugs kept GLM-5.3-Flash from running usefully under pipeline parallelism. Both fixes are hardware-agnostic (pure Python model/loader code, no kernels touched).

### 1. Pipeline parallelism was gated off (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py`)

`Glm5NextModel` shipped without `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`, so `supports_pp()` was `False` for `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` and `--pipeline-parallel-size > 1` was rejected. The in-tree comments spelled out why: *"PP is gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash (no make_empty_intermediate_tensors)"*.

The obstacle is mHC (manifold-constrained hyper-connections). Each token carries `config.mhc_num_residual_streams` (4) residual streams, and every decoder layer **defers** its `hc_post` mix into the *next* layer's fused post+pre kernel, returning `(x, residual, post, comb)` (`Glm5NextDecoderLayer.forward`). At a stage boundary there is no next layer to fuse with, so the deferred `post`/`comb` had nowhere to go and were simply dropped.

This PR resolves the deferred state at the boundary rather than propagating it:

* `Glm5NextModel.__init__` now installs `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`. For mHC it is the new `_make_empty_mhc_intermediate_tensors`: a single `"hidden_states"` key of shape `(batch, mhc_num_residual_streams, hidden_size)` — the residual streams themselves, token dim leading so the runner's per-batch slicing works. For non-mHC configs it is the standard `make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(["hidden_states", "residual"], hidden_size)`.
* `Glm5NextModel.forward` materializes the pending `hc_post` on the **sending** rank, through the last active layer's `hc_post()`, before constructing the `IntermediateTensors`. Only the residual streams cross the boundary. Under sequence parallelism the streams are flattened, all-gathered and reshaped (collectives expect 2-D), mirroring what the last rank already does before its final norm.
* On the **receiving** rank `residual`/`post`/`comb` start as `None`, so its first layer takes the standalone `hc_pre` path — which is exactly the layer-0 path minus `hc_expand` (`layer_idx != 0` there, so no re-expansion).
* `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` alias `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` so `supports_pp()` is satisfied. `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration.forward`, which the multimodal class inherits, already passes `intermediate_tensors` through to `language_model.model` and returns them unchanged on non-last ranks.

**Why this is equivalent:** `MHCFusedPostPreOp` is defined as `hc_post` followed by `hc_pre` on the updated streams. Splitting the two halves across a stage boundary computes the same two operations with the same parameters; only the kernel fusion is lost, for one layer per stage.

### 2. MTP drafter ran with an uninitialised embedding under PP (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`)

With PP enabled, MTP accepted **exactly zero** draft tokens. Outputs remained correct (verification is untouched), so MTP was pure overhead. Three things lined up:

* The checkpoint has no `layers.45.embed_tokens`; the MTP input embedding is the target's `model.embed_tokens.weight`.
* `Glm5NextMTP.load_weights` dropped that weight — the name arrives with the `model.language_model.` prefix already stripped, and `get_spec_layer_idx_from_weight_name` returns `None` for it.
* `maybe_share_target_embed` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py`) early-returns when `pp_world_size > 1` and the drafter does not declare `has_own_embed_tokens`; and on the last PP stage the target's `embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` anyway, so there is nothing to alias.

`Glm5NextMTP.__init__` now sets `self.has_own_embed_tokens = not get_pp_group().is_first_rank`, and `load_weights` loads `model.embed_tokens.weight` into the drafter's own `VocabParallelEmbedding` when that flag is set. With PP=1 the flag is `False`, the weight is skipped as before, and the target's embedding is aliased — no second copy, no behaviour change.

## Test Plan

* New CPU-only unit test `tests/models/glm5next/test_pp_intermediate_tensors.py` (no GPU, no process group, no weights): `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` keys/shapes/dtypes for mHC and non-mHC, and the `Glm5NextModel.forward` PP branch wiring on first/middle/last ranks with a patched `get_pp_group` and stand-in layers — including that exactly the last active layer's `hc_post` is called at a send, and that `supports_pp()` holds for both model classes.

  ```bash
  pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_pp_intermediate_tensors.py -q
  ```

* Standalone kernel-level comparison of `MHCPreOp` / `MHCPostOp` / `MHCFusedPostPreOp`: fused path vs. the split (post-then-pre) path used at a stage boundary.

* End-to-end serving on 4x NVIDIA CMP 170HX (GA100, sm_80, 64 GB) with `--pipeline-parallel-size 4`, checkpoint `canada-quant/GLM-5.3-Flash-W4A16-MTP`, vLLM `a31ec3a68`:
    * greedy free-form generation, coherence check;
    * GSM8K, first 50 test problems, greedy, chat template, with and without MTP;
    * `SpecDecoding` metrics with `num_speculative_tokens` 1 and 2, eager and CUDA-graph;
    * single-stream 256-token latency with and without MTP.

## Test Result

Unit test: `9 passed`. `ruff format` and `ruff check` clean on the three changed files, along with the `check-spdx-header`, `check-forbidden-imports`, `check-torch-cuda-call`, `check-root-lazy-imports` and `check-boolean-context-manager` pre-commit hooks.

Kernel-level fused-vs-split comparison: **bit-identical** residual streams for token counts > 32 (where the fused op already runs unfused internally); for <= 32 tokens, where the TileLang fused kernel keeps fp32 state, <= 1 bf16 ulp on `x` (max absolute difference 3.1e-2 at |x| ~ 4.7) and ~1e-3 on the mixes.

End-to-end at PP=4:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| PP=4 serving | refused (`supports_pp()` False) | works end to end, coherent greedy output |
| GSM8K (50 problems, greedy, chat) | n/a | **0.98** with MTP and without |
| SpecDecoding, N=1 and N=2, eager and CUDA-graph | `Accepted: 0 tokens, Drafted: 604+` | mean acceptance length **2.45–2.81** |
| per-position acceptance | 0 | **0.85 / 0.60** free-form, **0.95 / 0.86** GSM8K |
| single-stream 256-token generation | ~5.7 s (no MTP) | ~3.3 s (MTP) |

GSM8K accuracy is identical with and without MTP, as expected since speculative verification is unchanged.

**Hardware note:** the end-to-end numbers were measured on sm_80 (CMP 170HX) with an out-of-tree sparse-attention backend for that architecture. **That backend is not part of this PR** and neither fix depends on it — both changes are plain Python in the model definition and the MTP weight loader, with no architecture-specific code, so they apply to any accelerator that can run GLM-5.3-Flash. The PP=4 end-to-end evidence is what the author had hardware for; reviewers with Hopper/Blackwell nodes may want to confirm the same acceptance rates there.

**AI assistance disclosure:** this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests, and validated the behaviour end to end on the hardware above. The commits carry `Co-authored-by:` trailers.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,232 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash pipeline-parallel stage boundary.
+
+The mHC configs carry ``mhc_num_residual_streams`` residual streams per token
+and defer each layer's ``hc_post`` mix into the next layer's fused post+pre
+kernel. At a PP boundary there is no next layer, so ``Glm5NextModel.forward``
+materializes the pending ``hc_post`` on the sending rank and ships only the
+residual streams; the receiving rank's first layer then takes the standalone
+``hc_pre`` path. These tests pin that wiring (and the shapes/keys of
+``make_empty_intermediate_tensors``) without weights, a process group or a GPU.
+"""
+
+import types
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+import vllm.models.glm5next.common.model as glm_model
+from vllm.model_executor.models.interfaces import supports_pp
+from vllm.model_executor.models.utils import make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory
+from vllm.sequence import IntermediateTensors
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.cpu_test, pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup]
+
+HIDDEN = 128
+N_STREAMS = 4
+NUM_TOKENS = 6
+LAST_LAYER = 44
+
+
+def _make_empty_mhc(batch_size: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> IntermediateTensors:
+    """Call the mHC factory against a stand-in carrying the attrs it reads."""
+    stub = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        mhc_num_residual_streams=N_STREAMS,
+        config=types.SimpleNamespace(hidden_size=HIDDEN),
+    )
+    return glm_model.Glm5NextModel._make_empty_mhc_intermediate_tensors(
+        stub, batch_size=batch_size, dtype=dtype, device=torch.device("cpu")
+    )
+
+
+def test_make_empty_intermediate_tensors_mhc():
+    out = _make_empty_mhc(17, torch.bfloat16)
+    assert isinstance(out, IntermediateTensors)
+    # A single key: the deferred hc_post state is materialized into the
+    # streams before the send, so no separate "residual" copy is needed.
+    assert list(out.tensors) == ["hidden_states"]
+    hidden_states = out["hidden_states"]
+    assert hidden_states.shape == (17, N_STREAMS, HIDDEN)
+    assert hidden_states.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert hidden_states.device == torch.device("cpu")
+    # The runner slices the buffer per batch, so tokens must lead.
+    assert out[:5]["hidden_states"].shape == (5, N_STREAMS, HIDDEN)
+
+
+def test_make_empty_intermediate_tensors_non_mhc():
+    factory = make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(
+        ["hidden_states", "residual"], HIDDEN
+    )
+    out = factory(batch_size=9, dtype=torch.float16, device=torch.device("cpu"))
+    assert list(out.tensors) == ["hidden_states", "residual"]
+    for key in ("hidden_states", "residual"):
+        assert out[key].shape == (9, HIDDEN)
+        assert out[key].dtype == torch.float16
+
+
+class _FakeLayer(nn.Module):
+    """Records what it receives; mimics the decoder layer's return contract."""
+
+    def __init__(self, layer_idx: int, is_last_layer: bool, mhc: bool):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layer_idx = layer_idx
+        self.is_last_layer = is_last_layer
+        self.mhc = mhc
+        self.seen: tuple | None = None
+        self.hc_post_calls = 0
+
+    def forward(self, positions, hidden_states, residual, post, comb):
+        self.seen = (hidden_states, residual, post, comb)
+        if not self.mhc:
+            return hidden_states + 1, hidden_states, None, None
+        if post is None:
+            # Standalone hc_pre: expand only at layer 0, the streams become
+            # the residual and the layer input is derived from them.
+            x = hidden_states
+            if self.layer_idx == 0:
+                x = x.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, N_STREAMS, -1).contiguous()
+            residual = x
+            x = residual[:, 0, :]
+        else:
+            # Fused post+pre: a 2-D layer input plus the 3-D streams.
+            assert hidden_states.dim() == 2
+            assert residual.dim() == 3
+            x = hidden_states
+        if self.is_last_layer:
+            return residual.mean(dim=1), None, None, None
+        num_tokens = residual.shape[0]
+        idx = float(self.layer_idx)
+        return (
+            x * 2,
+            residual,
+            torch.full((num_tokens, N_STREAMS, 1), idx),
+            torch.full((num_tokens, N_STREAMS, N_STREAMS), idx),
+        )
+
+    def hc_post(self, x, residual, post, comb):
+        self.hc_post_calls += 1
+        return residual + x.unsqueeze(1)
+
+
+def _build_model(mhc: bool, layer_ids: list[int]) -> glm_model.Glm5NextModel:
+    model = glm_model.Glm5NextModel.__new__(glm_model.Glm5NextModel)
+    nn.Module.__init__(model)
+    model.mhc = mhc
+    model.mhc_num_residual_streams = N_STREAMS
+    model.config = types.SimpleNamespace(hidden_size=HIDDEN)
+    model.is_sequence_parallel = False
+    model._active_layers = [_FakeLayer(i, i == LAST_LAYER, mhc) for i in layer_ids]
+    model.norm = lambda hidden_states: hidden_states * 10
+    model.embed_tokens = lambda input_ids: torch.zeros(
+        input_ids.shape[0], HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    return model
+
+
+def _run_rank(model, *, is_first: bool, is_last: bool, intermediate_tensors):
+    pp_group = types.SimpleNamespace(is_first_rank=is_first, is_last_rank=is_last)
+    input_ids = torch.zeros(NUM_TOKENS, dtype=torch.long) if is_first else None
+    with mock.patch.object(glm_model, "get_pp_group", return_value=pp_group):
+        return model(input_ids, torch.arange(NUM_TOKENS), intermediate_tensors)
+
+
+def _streams() -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.randn(NUM_TOKENS, N_STREAMS, HIDDEN, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def test_middle_rank_materializes_pending_hc_post():
+    model = _build_model(True, [10, 11, 12])
+    streams = _streams()
+    out = _run_rank(
+        model,
+        is_first=False,
+        is_last=False,
+        intermediate_tensors=IntermediateTensors({"hidden_states": streams}),
+    )
+
+    first = model._active_layers[0]
+    # The received streams go in as-is and the first layer takes the
+    # standalone hc_pre path (no deferred state to fuse).
+    assert first.seen[0] is streams
+    assert first.seen[1:] == (None, None, None)
+
+    assert list(out.tensors) == ["hidden_states"]
+    assert out["hidden_states"].shape == (NUM_TOKENS, N_STREAMS, HIDDEN)
+    assert out["hidden_states"].dtype == streams.dtype
+    # Exactly the last active layer materializes its deferred hc_post.
+    assert model._active_layers[-1].hc_post_calls == 1
+    assert all(layer.hc_post_calls == 0 for layer in model._active_layers[:-1])
+    x_last = streams[:, 0, :] * 2 ** len(model._active_layers)
+    assert torch.equal(out["hidden_states"], streams + x_last.unsqueeze(1))
+
+
+def test_first_rank_embeds_and_sends_streams():
+    model = _build_model(True, [0, 1])
+    out = _run_rank(model, is_first=True, is_last=False, intermediate_tensors=None)
+
+    first = model._active_layers[0]
+    assert first.seen[0].dim() == 2  # embeddings, expanded inside layer 0
+    assert first.seen[1:] == (None, None, None)
+    assert list(out.tensors) == ["hidden_states"]

🚀

Cross-reference for maintainers: #57121 addresses the same starting point (`Glm5NextForCausalLM` advertises `SupportsPP` without `make_empty_intermediate_tensors`) from the other direction, by dropping `SupportsPP` so PP is rejected at config validation.

The two are alternatives rather than a conflict. #57121 makes the current "PP gated off" intent enforceable; this PR removes the reason for the gate by materializing the deferred mHC `post`/`comb` state at stage boundaries (with a unit test that checks the boundary output against the fused single-stage path) and fixing the MTP drafter embedding under PP. If this one is preferred, #57121's registry test would need `Glm5NextForCausalLM` back in the PP-supported set; if #57121 is preferred, the drafter-embedding half of this PR (`mtp.py`) is still independently useful once PP is re-enabled later. Happy to rebase either way.
